issues.title: Callback URL allowlist cannot admit custom-scheme deep links and fails silently
issues.verdict_note: Confirmed at HEAD: the only acceptance paths are a same-origin relative path or a WHATWG origin match. Also note that even an admitted deep link would receive only a Set-Cookie on a 302, so this fix is only useful together with MNA-003's native return leg (decision ticket 17).

evidence.note: A custom-scheme URL (myapp://cb) parses with origin 'null', so it can never match an https allowlist entry and silently falls back, with no log.

fix.summary: Add an explicit native-redirect allowlist matched on the full serialized scheme+authority(+path prefix) for non-http(s) URLs, and log when a requested callbackURL is discarded.
steps: packages/oauth/src/OAuth.ts `OAuthConfigShape`: add `readonly nativeRedirectURLs: ReadonlyArray<string>` (default `[]`), with entries like `myapp://oauth/callback` or `com.example.app:/cb` (RFC 8252 §7.1 private-use schemes).

Document the RFC 8252 guidance in packages/oauth/README.md: prefer claimed https universal/app links, and use private-use schemes only with the exchange-code leg.

issues.verdict_note: Confirmed. Canonical for JR-003 and OAP-003 (same schema, same fix shape). The three reports disagree on the outcome's shape (uniform OAuthCallbackFailed vs a typed provider-error outcome), so that choice is recorded as an open decision.

steps: packages/oauth/src/OAuthApi.ts CallbackQuery: `code: Schema.optional(Schema.String)`, plus `error: Schema.optional(Schema.String)`, `error_description: Schema.optional(Schema.String)` and `error_uri: Schema.optional(Schema.String)`.
packages/oauth/src/OAuth.ts OAuthShape.callback input: `code: string | undefined` and `error: string | undefined`.

callback: keep the rate limit, provider lookup, state/cookie check and `verification.consume` first (consuming the flow makes the denied flow single-use). Then, if `error !== undefined` or `code === undefined`, fail per the decision (B: OAuthAuthorizationDenied with the enumerated code, else OAuthCallbackFailed). Never call exchangeCode.
(B) OAuthApi.ts: add the OAuthAuthorizationDenied TaggedError (400) to the callback error list.
Handler: pass `query.error` through. Do not log error_description at more than debug level.

'error=access_denied with a mismatched state answers 400 OAuthCallbackFailed'
'the flow is consumed by a denial, so a replay with a code fails'

State is validated on the error path too (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1).

decision_options: A: any `error` param (after state+cookie validation and flow consumption) becomes the same field-less OAuthCallbackFailed (400). Strictly uniform (JR-003/OAP-003).

B: a new typed `OAuthAuthorizationDenied { error: Literals(['access_denied','invalid_request','unauthorized_client','unsupported_response_type','invalid_scope','server_error','temporarily_unavailable']) }` (400), raised only after the state+cookie check passes. error_description and error_uri are never echoed (provider-controlled free text). An unknown error code maps to OAuthCallbackFailed.
C: B, plus redirect to flow.callbackURL with `?error=<code>` instead of JSON.
issues.recommendation: B. The `error` code is already visible to the user in the redirect URL, so echoing the enumerated code after state validation reveals nothing to an attacker (they cannot forge a valid state+cookie pair for the victim). It lets apps render 'you cancelled' vs 'something went wrong', the most common non-attack callback outcome. Keep JSON, not a redirect (C), consistent with OAuthApi.ts's documented typed-error convention.

RBS-008 is already fixed and listed for completeness. CSS-006 and PDR-004 share one appendPreResponseHandler.

workstreams.title: Account-linking trust decisions and AccountExists accuracy
workstreams.rationale: All concern what the callback does when an email already exists or a new user is JIT-created. TMS-007 must land before AOMS-007: marking OAuth-created users verified is only safe once auto-link also requires a verified local account.

workstreams.title: Required baseUrl and operational docs
workstreams.rationale: Both are about baseUrl being defaulted silently and undocumented.

workstreams.title: Remaining provider-token persistence gap (id_token)
workstreams.rationale: BE-002 (e773cf1) closed refresh and expiry. Only the id_token column is left.

workstreams.title: Native/mobile OAuth return leg (decision ticket 17)
workstreams.rationale: The native return leg (exchange code plus token endpoint) and the deep-link callback allowlist are only useful together. Shares ticket 17 and the bearer-delivery DTO with MNA-001 (slice 07).

workstreams.title: Per-organization OAuth connections (decision ticket 18)
workstreams.rationale: One decision covers both. Cross-slice with EP-001 and DRS-001 (slice 05, tenant key) and packages/organization (slice 08).

workstreams.title: client_credentials in packages/api-key (decision ticket 10)
workstreams.rationale: Owned by the api-key slice (09). Recorded here only because the audit anchored it to OAuth.ts. packages/oauth does not change.

workstreams.title: Document the users/accounts transaction-domain invariant
workstreams.rationale: A spec-only fix, linked to the residency findings in slice 05.

workstreams.title: callbackURL open-redirect (closed)
workstreams.rationale: All closed by 9b3e42c. The remaining deep-link work lives in native-session-bootstrap.

workstreams.title: Path-parameter naming rule (cross-slice, AVS-006 canonical)
workstreams.rationale: A duplicate of slice 10's AVS-006. No oauth change is needed under the proposed rule.
